=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:34-35 (with .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:43-45; scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1200-1235) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The audit assumes a bundle's tracking issue names every bundled plan, but the hand-off does not require the project summary to keep each plan path, and build_tracking_issue_body does not write project_description.
  WHY: A later /audit-plans run may miss in-flight bundle members and re-recommend a plan or recommend a colliding one. Reviewers rated this MAJOR, which is mapped here to high.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:36-41 (with implement-plan-ai.md:43-44) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A candidate can join a bundle through a dependency or shared file even when its declared prerequisite is outside the bundle (in flight, screened out or unmerged), and the conflict screen does not check this.
  WHY: The member's phases would run on a base branch that lacks the prerequisite code. Severity disagreement: z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rated it NIT, the others MAJOR, so the highest is used.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:36-39 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The relatedness test counts any overlapping touched files as related, while the conflict screen at line 36 lets plans that share only independent files pass, so plans that share only such a file can be bundled.
  WHY: This contradicts "Unrelated plans are never bundled", and a model following the text literally may over-bundle.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:8,43,74 (with audit-plans.md:40) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The 8-phase cap relies on counting only missing phases, but implement-plan-ai has no plan-status classification step, and duplicate plan paths in $ARGUMENTS are not handled.
  WHY: The cap can be applied to an arbitrary count, and a duplicated path could count one plan twice.
- tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:84-114 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The tests assert "more than 8 phases in total" but not the phase-counting wording ("a plan with no phase split counts as 1", "a partially-implemented plan counts only the phases still missing").
  WHY: That wording can be edited or weakened without a test failing, so the audit and the hand-off can drift on how phases are counted.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md (mirrored in workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md) lines 34-35, with .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md lines 43-45 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The bundle gate says the tracking issue names 2–3 plans, but build_tracking_issue_body (scripts/orchestrate_lib.py lines 1200-1235) does not write project_description, and the hand-off does not require the summary to keep each plan path.
  WHY: A later audit may not set aside the other bundled plans and can recommend an in-flight or colliding plan.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md (mirrored in the template copy) lines 39-41 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A member's declared prerequisite that lies outside the bundle (in flight, screened out or unmerged) is not covered, and the conflict screen at line 36 checks only file overlap.
  WHY: A member can run as if its prerequisite had landed on the base branch.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md (mirrored in the template copy) line 40 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The "Related" bullet counts any touched-file overlap, while line 36 lets shared but independent files pass.
  WHY: This contradicts "Unrelated plans are never bundled" and can lead to over-bundling.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md (mirrored in the template copy) line 8 and line 74 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The 8-phase cap uses missing-phase counts, but implement-plan-ai has no step that classifies plan status, and duplicate paths in $ARGUMENTS are not handled.
  WHY: The missing-phase count is an unguided judgement for a direct invocation, and a duplicated path could produce a "bundle" of one plan dispatched twice.
- HARDENING: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py lines 105-114 (`test_implement_plan_ai_dispatches_a_bundle_once`, `test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps`) do not pin the phase-counting wording at audit-plans.md:40 and implement-plan-ai.md:8, 43, 74. The suggested fix is 2-3 added asserts, plus one clause requiring the project summary to name every plan path and one clause rejecting duplicate plan paths. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:34 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The bundle-aware footprint step assumes the tracking issue keeps every bundled plan name, but build_tracking_issue_body (scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1200-1235) writes only the LLM-generated project_summary and the wave list, and parse_tracking_body (scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:3088-3134) has no field for plan paths.
  WHY: If the summary drops member paths, a later audit reads only one plan and can recommend a colliding or already in-flight member.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:39 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The dependency clause lets a candidate join the bundle without checking that its prerequisite plan is in the bundle, in flight, screened out or unstarted.
  WHY: A member whose prerequisite was screened out at line 36 can still pass the conflict screen and be bundled, so the orchestrator ships phases on a base that lacks the prerequisite code.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:36 (read with line 39) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The conflict screen lets plans sharing independent files pass, but the relatedness test counts any overlapping touched files as related.
  WHY: Two independent plans that append different rows to the same doc table can be bundled, contradicting "Unrelated plans are never bundled".
- tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:84-114 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: No new test asserts the phase-counting phrases that appear at audit-plans.md:40 and implement-plan-ai.md:8, 43 and 74.
  WHY: The phrases can be deleted or weakened without a test failing, and the audit and hand-off can count phases differently.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:43-45; .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:34-35 (tracking body built by scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1207-1235) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The audit assumes the tracking issue names every bundled plan, but the hand-off does not require the decomposer to keep each plan path in the project summary, and the tracking-issue builder does not retain the original project description.
  WHY: A later audit cannot identify an omitted member as in flight or add its declared files, so it can recommend the same plan again or conflicting work.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:39-41; .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:43-44 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A candidate can qualify for a bundle through shared files while its prerequisite outside the bundle is unsatisfied, and the hand-off only adds dependencies between bundled plans.
  WHY: The dependent phase runs without the prerequisite implementation or a DAG edge that waits for it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md (mirrored in workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md) lines 34-35, cross-ref .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md lines 43-45 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The bundle in-flight gate assumes the tracking issue keeps every bundled plan's path, but build_tracking_issue_body (scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:1200-1235) writes only the free-form project_summary (prompts/mode-orchestrate.txt:137), wave titles and dependency edges.
  WHY: If the summary omits a member path, a later audit sees only the first-named plan and can recommend the other member or a colliding plan as a new project.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md (mirrored in the template copy) lines 8, 43, 74 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The 8-phase cap depends on counting "the phases still missing", but implement-plan-ai has no plan-status classification step.
  WHY: The cap cannot be computed correctly for a partial plan at dispatch time, so a bundle can exceed the real budget or be rejected wrongly.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md (mirrored in the template copy) line 39 vs line 36 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The relatedness test accepts overlapping touched files, while the conflict screen lets shared but independent files pass with a note.
  WHY: Two plans that only append distinct rows to the same doc table qualify as related and are bundled although independent.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md (mirrored in the template copy) lines 39-41 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A member's declared prerequisite outside the bundle (in flight, screened out or unmerged) is unhandled, and the conflict screen at line 36 checks only touched-file overlap.
  WHY: Those PRs build on a base that lacks the prerequisite and fail or collide.
- HARDENING: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py (`test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps` lines 92-97, `test_implement_plan_ai_dispatches_a_bundle_once` lines 105-114) do not pin the phase-counting wording at audit-plans.md line 40 and implement-plan-ai.md lines 8, 43, 74. The suggested fix is asserts for "a plan with no phase split counts as 1" and "a partially-implemented plan counts only the phases still missing" (about 4 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
- HARDENING: implement-plan-ai.md step 1 "Bundle." bullet (line 8) does not reject duplicate plan paths in $ARGUMENTS. The suggested fix is one sentence on deduplicating paths and falling back to the single-plan path when fewer than 2 distinct plans remain (about 2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
